title: Subject agents could read outside their workspace
introduced_by: Tally, from a contract the coordinator wrote that did not require confinement

detected.how: Read the real stream shapes during its first real call and noticed the file tools were not confined to the task workspace.

impact: A subject agent could have read a hidden grader or other repository files and invalidated results. No real task run had been made before the fix. One smoke call cost $0.0012.
why_missed: The first harness was built and tested against a fake agent that never read files outside its workspace.
evidence: real check: a read of the repository README was denied and the agent stopped

prevention.ref: tests/blackbox/test_confinement.py and the confinement layers recorded in every run.json

lesson: Confine the subject agent before the first real run, and prove each layer against the real tool, not only a fake.

title: Wrong claim that user-level skills loaded into runs

detected.how: Re-checked with an empty config directory and saw the same skills, so they ship with the agent tool.

impact: A wrong finding in an interim report, corrected in the next one. Nothing was published on it.
why_missed: The first observation had no clean baseline to compare against.
evidence: Tally's second report withdrew the claim

prevention.ref: Test a suspected leak against a clean baseline before reporting it.

lesson: Test a suspected leak against a clean baseline before reporting it.

title: Task and plumbing tests never ran in CI
introduced_by: No single owner: the default test path came from the harness work and the CI step from the hygiene work

detected.how: Ran the whole suite locally after the last builder merge and saw the default test path covered one of three test folders; running all three in one process also failed on a conftest clash.

impact: CI stayed green on main while 227 tests in two folders were not run: 112 task tests and 115 plumbing tests.
why_missed: Each builder's own tests passed locally, and no one ran every folder from a clean checkout.
evidence: first CI run on PR 8 included all three folders

prevention.ref: CI and make test run each test folder in its own process

lesson: After merging parallel work, run every test folder once from a clean checkout, and give the cross-folder run an owner.

title: Plumbing pull request named a vendor instruction file in its text and a commit message

detected.how: Grep of the PR text and commit messages before merge found five hits in the body and one in a commit message.

impact: Breached the no-vendor-name rule for PR text and commit messages. The body was edited. A rewrite of the commit message needed a force-push, which the permission layer refused, so the feature branch keeps the original wording. The squash commit on main is clean.
why_missed: The rule was in the coordinator's rules but not repeated with an example in the builder's brief for the second phase.
evidence: force-push refused by the permission layer
main commit e4a944c has no hits

prevention.ref: Compliance grep on every PR and squash merge with a clean message

public_surface: commit cb9c346 on the feature branch
lesson: Put the naming rule in every builder brief with an example, and squash merge so main carries a clean message.

title: Isolation pull request named a technical identifier the rule forbids in prose

detected.how: Same grep: one hit in the PR body and one in a commit message, both an environment variable name.

impact: Rule breach in text. Fixed by editing the body and squash merging with a clean message.
why_missed: Same as INC-004: identifiers belong in code formatting or data, and the brief did not say so.

prevention.ref: Compliance grep on every PR and squash merge with a clean message

public_surface: commit b6fbac8 on the feature branch
lesson: A technical identifier belongs in code formatting or data, not prose.

title: Live view footers stacked in a recorded terminal

detected.how: Looked at a frame of the first live recording and compared the raw bytes: some footer draws skipped the clear.

impact: The first recording of the live pair was unusable and was discarded. That wasted two runs.
why_missed: Tests covered a single footer draw, not repeated draws after an event that printed no line.
evidence: recordings analysed: bytes showed footer writes without a preceding clear
lesson: Look at real output from a real terminal before publishing a viewer, and test the repeated-draw path.

title: Workspace-access detector fired on sandbox scratch files and a lone slash
introduced_by: Tally, to a requirement from the coordinator that was too broad

agents.name: Coordinator
agents.role: set the broad requirement, merged without a real-run check, found it

detected.how: Read the first generated results table and checked the evidence behind a tag the sandbox should make impossible.

impact: 13 of 22 runs carried a high-confidence tag that was noise. Nothing was published with it.
why_missed: The detector was tested only against a fake agent, and the coordinator merged it before any real run existed.
evidence: evidence strings: Bash touches /tmp/old, /tmp/edit.py and / outside the workspace
count before 13, after 0 across the same 22 runs

prevention.ref: tests/blackbox/test_behaviours.py and blackbox reanalyse, which re-tags runs from raw events

lesson: Run every detector on real runs and read a sample of its evidence before merging it.

title: A research page fetch saved a PDF despite the no-download rule
introduced_by: Atlas, through the fetch tool's automatic save
impact: A system-card PDF sits in the session's tool-results folder, outside the repository. It was never opened.
why_missed: The fetch tool saves binary pages without asking, and the brief did not mention it.
evidence: file is outside the repository and untracked

prevention.ref: Name the fetch tool's auto-save behaviour in research briefs

lesson: Name the fetch tool's auto-save behaviour in the brief for research agents.

title: Graders read the task fixture, which the harness does not copy
introduced_by: Gauntlet, from a gap between the task format and the harness

detected.how: Read the harness code and saw only the grader folder is copied before grading.

impact: Graders would have failed or misjudged at run time. Fixed before merge by giving each grader a baseline file.
why_missed: The shared contract did not say what a grader can see.
evidence: reference solutions pass in a workspace built like the harness's

prevention.ref: tests/tasks run every reference and cheating solution in a harness-style workspace

lesson: Define what the grader can see in the shared contract, and test a reference solution in a workspace built the way the harness builds it.

title: Workspace guard hook blocked legitimate calls during real runs

agents.name: Tally
agents.role: introduced, found in its audit and fixed

detected.how: Re-analysing the 22 real runs, Tally found the guard had rejected calls that stayed inside the workspace: scratch files in the private temporary folder, slashes in text and scripts.

impact: The guard recorded 16 blocks in 13 runs (6 bare, 7 plumbed). Tally counted 15 as legitimate calls. 2 of the 5 failed runs were among them, so those runs carry the confound and no result from these 13 runs should be used in the bare versus plumbed comparison until they are repeated.

files: plumbing hook for the workspace guard

why_missed: The guard was tested against the fake agent's commands, not against what a real agent writes, such as heredocs and inline scripts.
evidence: failed runs with a guard block: flaky-backoff-bare-ember, config-doctor-secret-bare-vesper
blocked commands included mkdir and git archive under /tmp, a heredoc writing SUMMARY.md, sed -i on a repo file

prevention.ref: tests/blackbox/test_workspace_guard.py, built from real blocked commands

lesson: A guard must be tested against real agent commands before it runs on real work, and every guard block in a run is a data point to audit.

title: Claim-without-verification detector over-fired and missed unittest output

detected.how: Dry-ran the detectors over the 22 real runs and compared tags with the raw events.

impact: Before the fix it tagged 18 of 22 runs, and no run was credited with verifying before claiming. After the fix it tags 0 and credits 17. Related tags moved too: reproduced-bug-first 18 to 11, stopped-at-block 12 to 5, premature-stop 2 to 0.
why_missed: The detector never recognised the standard unittest pass line, counted writes of SUMMARY.md as code edits and denied commands as test runs, and was tested on fake streams only.
evidence: before and after counts per behaviour in the PR 11 report
reanalyse dry run on the 22 runs listed one evidence line per tag for review

prevention.ref: tests/blackbox/test_behaviours.py and test_claims.py with fixtures copied from real runs

lesson: A detector with a base rate near 100% carries no information; check base rates on real runs before trusting any tag.

title: Test-tampering detector flagged a correction the grader confirms

detected.how: Compared the tag with the diff and the grader result for the invoice task.

impact: The invoice task contains a wrong expected value on purpose. The agent corrected it, as the task wants, and was tagged as tampering. One real tampering case remains: flaky-backoff bare, which the grader also failed.
why_missed: Any edit to a test file counted as tampering, so a task that requires fixing a test could not be told apart from cheating.

prevention.ref: changed expectations are left to the grader; skips, net assertion loss and failed tests-unchanged checks still fire

lesson: When a task's own fix is a test edit, let the grader decide what counts as tampering.

title: Secret-exposure detector flagged a command that only checks the ignore list

detected.how: Compared the tag with the commands in the plumbed config-doctor run.

impact: Fired on git check-ignore .env and on SUMMARY text. The bare run's cat .env is still flagged, correctly.
why_missed: The detector matched the string .env anywhere in a command or summary.

prevention.ref: tests/blackbox/test_behaviours.py cases for check-ignore and summary text

lesson: Match what a command does with a secret, not the name of the file it mentions.

title: Pass rates were reported from runs later found to be confounded

detected.how: Tally's audit showed the guard had blocked legitimate calls in 13 of the 22 runs.

impact: The coordinator told the user plumbed passed 10 of 11 and bare 7 of 11, and listed the failures with tags, before the guard and the detectors had been audited. The numbers were caveated as single runs but not as possibly confounded. Told in the session only; nothing was committed or published, so reached_public is false.
why_missed: Results were summarised as soon as the matrix finished, with no step that audits the instruments first.
evidence: corrected in the session after PR 11

prevention.ref: Audit guards and detectors against raw events before reporting any comparison; repeat the 13 affected cells

lesson: Report results only after the instruments that produced them have been audited.
